block_size doesn’t change it (tried 64, the e2e-test value). Local workaround: for hisparse_resident layers, emit per-cache regions (cache.data_ptr(), physical_page_size, row_stride) instead. This may not be the right general fix (see finding 3).
2. Host-pool NIXL registration includes unpinned slop → UCX “already mapped” (startup crash).
allocate_pinned_host_pool over-allocates padded_size + page and cudaHostRegisters only the page-aligned slice, but register_region records the whole backing storage in _host_registration_ranges. UCX’s cuda_copy MD then cuMemHostRegisters a range that overlaps the already-pinned middle and fails hard:

UCX ERROR cuMemHostRegister_v2(...) failed: part or all of the requested memory range is already mapped
nixl_cu13._bindings.nixlBackendError: NIXL_ERR_BACKEND

UCX ERROR cuMemHostRegister_v2(...) failed: part or all of the requested memory range is already mapped
nixl_cu13._bindings.nixlBackendError: NIXL_ERR_BACKEND

Reproduces at any host_pool_gib (tried 4 and 24). Local workaround: shrink each recorded range to the pinned sub-range (base + (-base % 4096), nbytes - 4096) before register_memory — UCX’s memory-type probe then dedupes. (Skipping the pool’s own pinning instead is rejected by the hisparse_backup kernel’s “host_cache must be pinned” check.)
3. Open correctness issue: long-prefix P/D transfers garble output on GLM shapes.
With the two workarounds above, the P/D fleet serves and short routed requests are byte-correct, but long-prefix requests (e.g. 40k-token prompt) return garbled text through the router while the same prompt direct-to-decode (local prefill) is coherent — i.e. multi-block transfer of hisparse KV corrupts data. This may well be my workaround for finding 1 mis-addressing blocks under _physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block packing rather than a bug in the stack itself — but either way the GLM packed-pool P/D path appears unexercised upstream. Happy to test a proper fix or provide more detail (logs, configs, exact geometry dumps).
Also worth a docs note: the NIXL handshake (Number of KV layers must match between prefill and decode) means hisparse_config must be enabled on both P/D roles, not just the decoder — enabling decode-only fails at the first transfer.

subclasses FlashAttentionBackend and does not override supports_batch_invariance(), so it
inherits return True from vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py. But the QSA implementation
does not use FlashAttention: Qwen3_8FlashNextQSAFlashAttentionImpl.forward_qsa calls the model’s
own qsa_sparse_paged_attention Triton kernel.
That kernel is not batch-invariant, and the reason is concrete — the split-K reduction depth is a
function of the number of query rows in the batch:

base_programs = (
  q.shape[0] * k_cache.shape[2]
)  # q.shape[0] = query rows in this batch
small_profile_limit = 8 if block_m <= 8 else 4
if base_programs <= small_profile_limit:
  block_n, target_splits, partial_warps = 16, 64, 4
elif base_programs < 32:
  block_n, target_splits, partial_warps = 16, 32, 4
elif base_programs <= 256:
  block_n, target_splits, partial_warps = 64, 8, 2
elif base_programs <= 512:
  block_n, target_splits, partial_warps = 64, 4, 2
else:
  block_n, target_splits, partial_warps = 64, 1, 2
...
num_splits = min(max_useful_splits, target_splits)
num_splits sets how many partial accumulators _qsa_merge_splitk_kernel combines. Crossing any
of those thresholds changes the reduction tree, and therefore changes the floating-point rounding
of the same request’s attention output. That is precisely what VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is supposed
to rule out.
Why this is currently latent, and why it will not stay that way
On this model the flag cannot be reached today: vllm/v1/attention/selector.py raises before the
attention backend is consulted, because the GDN/mamba backend does not declare batch invariance:

if (
  envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
  and not mamba_attn_backend.supports_batch_invariance()
):
  raise RuntimeError(
    f'VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for {mamba_attn_backend.get_name()}.'
  )
So the incorrect claim is masked by an unrelated guard. The moment mamba/GDN gains batch-invariance
support (#48613 tracks exactly that), this model would start up with
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 and silently produce batch-dependent results — the failure mode the
flag exists to prevent. A backend-level capability claim that is only true by accident of a
neighbouring guard is worth fixing before it becomes load-bearing.
Suggestions

One line, immediate: override supports_batch_invariance() to return False on
Qwen3_8FlashNextQSAFlashAttentionBackend. AttentionBackend already defaults to False; the
True is inherited only because the class reuses FlashAttentionBackend for its metadata
builder.
If QSA should support the flag: make the profile selection independent of q.shape[0] when
vllm_is_batch_invariant() is set — pin (block_n, target_splits, partial_warps) to one
profile so num_splits no longer depends on batch composition.

Option 1 is the correct default: declaring False costs nothing but an error message, while
declaring True wrongly costs silent numerical divergence.

#54015 [Kimi-K3] Merge MLA gate into QKV-A projection
vllm-project/vllm#54015 · gau-nernst · MERGED · created 2026-08-27T07:44:15Z · merged 2026-08-28T00:47:19Z
Purpose
This PR merges MLA’s g_proj (used for output gating) into QKV_a projection to create a larger GEMM. We don’t expect this to have a large impact as the original QKV_a gemm is already quite large. The main purpose of this PR is to prepare for the upcoming fused AG-GEMM (used in SP), which benefits significantly from having a larger GEMM.
What makes this PR a bit more complicated is that currently we have a low-latency optimization for MLA: g_proj runs in a side stream when bs<512, so that g_proj can overlap with qkv_a_proj+MLA. From my testing, this side-stream optimization is faster than running a combined qkv_a_g_proj GEMM at bs=1, hence we should still keep this optimization.
To do so, this PR does weight slicing when bs<512 to run g_proj in side stream, preserving the current behavior. When bs>=512, the merged GEMM replaces the sequential GEMM baseline.
Dispatch logic

Entrypoint: forward()

Q full rank (Kimi-Linear): _forward_full_rank_q. This is unchanged, because Kimi-Linear doesn’t use output gate
Q low-rank (Kimi-K3): _forward_q_lora

When running g_proj in side stream is eligible (M<512, BF16 weights): slice weight and run (qkv_a+MLA) || (g)
Otherwise, run qkv_a_g together





Limitations:

Entrypoint: forward()

Q full rank (Kimi-Linear): _forward_full_rank_q. This is unchanged, because Kimi-Linear doesn’t use output gate
Q low-rank (Kimi-K3): _forward_q_lora

When running g_proj in side stream is eligible (M<512, BF16 weights): slice weight and run (qkv_a+MLA) || (g)
Otherwise, run qkv_a_g together





Limitations:

Since we do weight slicing here, we must handle each quantization explicitly (i.e. for quantized weights, need to slice the scale factors as well. Also need to manually dispatch the GEMM function, can’t rely on Linear module).
This PR currently only supports BF16 weight slicing (official Kimi-K3 weights). In other words, if QKV_a and g_proj are not BF16, running g_proj in side stream is disabled. This may LL perf of 3rd party quantizations, such as nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4. We can expand support as needed cc @wzhao18
bs<512 threshold might not be optimal. This PR does not re-tune this threshold.

vllm-project/vllm#54255 · djmmoss · MERGED · created 2026-08-28T19:17:50Z · merged 2026-10-01T02:28:51Z

For supported pure speculative-decode batches, this replaces separate short
convolution, recurrent KDA, and gated normalization launches with
flashinfer.packed_fused_kda_decode. Unsupported configurations and mixed

disabled are all required. The recurrent state may be float32 or bfloat16;
bfloat16 needs flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5503.

#54261 [Kimi-K3][Perf] Make native CUDA AttnRes the SM100 default
vllm-project/vllm#54261 · zyongye · MERGED · created 2026-08-28T19:46:08Z · merged 2026-08-31T23:18:12Z
Purpose
Make the native CUDA Kimi-K3 AttnRes implementation the default for dense
hidden_size=7168 inputs on SM100.
This PR:

extends the existing register/TMEM kernel to cover block counts 0 through 8,
optional prefix addition, optional output normalization, and block-bank
writes;
uses the existing source-chunk schedule for all supported block counts,
while preserving a compile-time-folded common path;
makes output normalization a compile-time specialization so the disabled
path elides its shared-memory buffer, barrier, and arithmetic;
delays the PDL wait until the first producer-dependent prefix or delta TMA
for every native shape and triggers dependents after the producer TMAs;
retains Triton as the fallback for unsupported devices and non-dense row
layouts; and
adds a reproducible CUDA-versus-Triton kernel benchmark.

Duplicate-work check: the author of #53524 coordinated moving its AttnRes PDL
handoff into this integrated change; that PR’s remaining distinct scope is its
C=1 MoE/router work. #50760 changes warmup profiles only. Neither otherwise
extends the native kernel to all Kimi-K3 AttnRes call variants.

#54371 [Qwen4Exp] Support UVA PLE-offload and Engram tensor parallelism
vllm-project/vllm#54371 · peakcrosser7 · MERGED · created 2026-08-29T18:32:53Z · merged 2026-09-09T14:32:35Z
Purpose
Add UVA-based PLE offload and Engram tensor parallelism (ETP) for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
--engram-config controls PLE weight storage and embedding sharding:

cpu_offload=true stores each local PLE weight shard in pinned CPU memory. The GPU reads the required rows directly through CUDA Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA), using a dedicated CUDA stream. Offload can also be enabled with VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1 when cpu_offload is omitted; an explicit cpu_offload value takes precedence.
cpu_offload=false keeps PLE weights on the GPU.
embedding_across_dp=false uses ETP=TP, keeping a separate TP-sharded PLE table in each DP replica.
embedding_across_dp=true uses ETP=TP×DP, sharding the PLE table across all DP replicas.

Offload and cross-DP sharding can be enabled independently. Both options default to false.
Design
The PLE embedding implementation is organized into three abstraction levels:

Qwen4ExpPLEDeviceEmbedding and Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding encapsulate device-specific allocation and execution. The pinned-host backend implements the asynchronous UVA path, while the device backend retains the resident lookup path.

Not a duplicate
Searched the open PRs for Qwen4Exp PLE offload, and PLE UVA.
There are related PRs, but they use materially different designs:

#53899 uses a dedicated CPU offload worker and transfers selected rows back to GPU workers. This PR keeps the table in process-local pinned memory and lets the GPU read the required rows directly through UVA, without an offload worker or IPC row transfer.
#54129 uses disk-backed mmap storage to reduce host-memory residency. This PR intentionally keeps the complete local shard pinned in RAM for direct UVA access.
#54431 optimizes ragged n-gram ID generation for the worker-based offload path.
#54517 fuses the PLE compute kernels and is orthogonal to the pinned-table storage, asynchronous UVA lookup, and NP topology introduced here.

#54448 [Core] Add XPress speculative decoding method
vllm-project/vllm#54448 · ZKBig · MERGED · created 2026-08-30T16:56:03Z · merged 2026-10-22T21:04:55Z
Purpose
Adds XPress, a causal refiner for block-diffusion drafters, as a V1 speculative decoding method alongside DFlash and DSpark. Paper: 2608.02438⁠ (Wang et al., 2026) 
A block-diffusion drafter such as DFlash proposes a whole block in one forward pass, which makes drafting cheap, and decodes it from per-position marginals, which makes it inaccurate: token k is drawn without seeing what the drafter chose at k-1. The target verifies conditionally, so blocks that are individually plausible but jointly improbable are rejected early, capping acceptance length.
Design
XPress adds a small head that reads the drafter’s per-position hidden state, a block-global summary and the previous token, fuses them into a rank-256 bottleneck, mixes across the block with a lower-triangular (causal) mixer, and reads back out as a bias on the base logits. Everything except the two vocabulary projections lives in the bottleneck (~80M params, 96% of
which are those two matrices).
Because the mixer is true causal rather than local smooth, the block is resolved by Jacobi iteration rather than a left-to right loop: the same call runs K times, each pass re-feeding the previous pass’s argmax, so the serial depth is a constant K instead of the block size. Both stages are fixed-shape and loop-free, so the whole draft step is CUDA-graph capturable, which is what makes K passes cheap: they cost K matmuls, not K kernel launches. Two Triton kernels keep a pass at three launches (xpress_latent_pass, and a fused add+argmax that writes straight into the block buffer so the [N, B, V] sum is never materialized).
XPressSpeculator subclasses DFlashSpeculator and overrides only draft generation; attention, KV cache setup and weight sharing are inherited unchanged. Existing files gain 39 lines of method registration; everything else is new files.
Test Plan

# e2e (80GB GPU; public Qwen3-8B + XPress checkpoint pair): full GSM8K at temperature 0,
# accuracy and acceptance metrics against reference values -- same protocol as the
# DFlash and DSpark tests in acceptance_rates/
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py -s
The e2e test guards GSM8K accuracy and acceptance rate and length against references, with an upper bound on acceptance length. Note that acceptance length moves by about 0.5% with anything that changes the vLLM config hash, because the hash keys torch.compile’s cache and autotuning then picks different kernels, shifting the floating-point reduction order so that near-tie draft tokens flip. Under enforce_eager=True the paths are identical.

#54513 [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Separate prefill and decode paths for QSA indexer
vllm-project/vllm#54513 · gau-nernst · MERGED · created 2026-08-31T06:19:57Z · merged 2026-09-02T01:08:10Z
Purpose
#53896 ships with a simple QSA indexer kernel that is used for both decode and prefill requests. This is not efficient as we can’t design kernels specialized for decode and prefill shapes separately. This PR splits a mixed batch into decode and prefill requests, so that efficient decode/prefill kernels can be invoked separately, similar to how other attention backends work in vLLM.
Currently this PR ships 2 decode/prefill-specialized Triton kernels to replace the original generic QSA indexer, but these are not meant to be SOL. Further optimizations are left for future PRs.
Main changes

Replace _qsa_mqa_paged_kernel with _qsa_mqa_paged_uniform_kernel (decode and spec-decode) and _qsa_mqa_paged_prefill_kernel (prefill). Create a new file qsa_indexer.py under NVIDIA ops.
Add visible_blocks = (logical_position + 1) // compress_ratio to QSA metadata. Previously this is computed by the indexer score kernel, which is not quite natural.
Add warmup logic for _qsa_mqa_paged_uniform_kernel. The prefill kernel only has 1 specialization, it doesn’t need warmup
Switch _LOGITS_WORKSPACE_BYTES to env var VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB, which raises the default workspace size from 128 MiB to 512 MiB. Decode kernel does not observe this limit, following DeepSeek sparse attention.

The kernels’ heuristics are currently tuned on GB300. They might not be optimal for all GPUs.

Correctness details
n-gram ID generation

Preserve PyTorch int64 overflow behavior. Overflow hashes may become negative, so the kernel explicitly normalizes modulo results to match torch.remainder, guaranteeing every ID remains within its head-specific range: [offset, offset + vocab_size).kernel
Ragged request boundaries are resolved from query_start_loc, including empty requests and non-power-of-two request counts. Tokens preceding the current chunk come from persistent n-gram context, and crossing EOS replaces all older suffix positions with EOS.

Dilated short-conv

Preserves cache semantics for decode, prefill, and speculative decode. Speculative state is rolled back by num_accepted_tokens - 1, while current candidate inputs are retained for the next target-model step.
Convolution output and cache writeback use separate kernels so state is not overwritten before all causal reads complete.
For mixed-spec/non-spec batches, token positions are looked up inside the kernel, eliminating separate gather/scatter ops.

PLE gate

Match PyTorch numerics exactly (cast intermediates to BF16 as appropriately)

#54687 [Kernel] Reuse Qwen4Exp HC combine-norm for MTP input
vllm-project/vllm#54687 · gcanlin · MERGED · created 2026-09-01T03:29:00Z · merged 2026-09-04T09:57:56Z
Summary

Reuse the existing Qwen4Exp HC combine kernels for MTP input instead of maintaining an MTP-only add-and-norm kernel.
Treat injection_logits=None as unit injection. Triton specializes directly on the optional inj_ptr, so the MTP path performs no injection load or sigmoid.
Pass fc_embedding into the normal decoder as a pending HC block output. The existing combine-norm kernel then fuses the BF16 broadcast add and grouped Gemma RMSNorm.
Generalize both HC combine variants to the same optional-injection contract, and remove _forward_mtp_layer plus the duplicated MTP kernel.

This does not duplicate #54560, which targets the general Qwen4Exp M=1 SM90 decode path; this change targets the MTP entry residual add and grouped RMSNorm for arbitrary token counts.
Data flow

target / feedback hidden                 new token
          |                                  |
 pre-norm + fc_hidden                embed + pre-norm
          |                                  |
 residual [T, HC, H]               fc_embedding [T, H]
          |                                  |
          |                         pending block output
          |                         injection = None
          +------------------+---------------+
                             |
                 Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer.forward
                             |
                  attn_hc.combine_and_mix
                             |
             hc_combine_norm[inj_ptr=None]
                    /                    \
       residual + embedding          grouped RMSNorm
                    \                    /
                     +--------+----------+
                              |
                  normal HC mix and decoder
                              |
                     Attention -> MLP
Final kernel specialization
Following review, the final implementation keeps the optional-pointer design while minimizing special-case code:

Residual and block loads are issued before FP32 conversion and arithmetic.
Gated and unit-injection paths share the same two-dimensional tiled layout and RMSNorm reduction.
Both paths use one flattened token-major launch grid, keeping the streams for each token adjacent without an injection-specific grid branch.
The only unit-injection-specific scheduling is issuing the norm-weight load before the reduction; the gated path keeps the load after the reduction to limit its live range.

#54713 [BugFix] Retain both replay boundaries so an EAGLE resend of a block-aligned prompt still hits
vllm-project/vllm#54713 · tobymao · MERGED · created 2026-09-01T06:25:25Z · merged 2026-09-10T08:39:25Z
Purpose
Follow-up to #53945, which fixed Mamba/SWA sparse-retention reuse under EAGLE/MTP by moving the replay boundary to where a lookup lands after the EAGLE drop:

aligned = (
  request.num_prompt_tokens // scheduler_block_size * scheduler_block_size
)
return max(aligned - scheduler_block_size, 0)
That is the right position for a sibling whose prompt merely starts with this one. It is not the right position for a resend of the identical prompt: get_computed_blocks caps a lookup at num_tokens - 1, because the last token has to be recomputed to obtain logits. So an identical resend matches one block lower and drops from there.
The two coincide unless the prompt length is an exact multiple of the scheduler block size — there they differ by exactly one block:

prompt (block 32)identical resend lands onlonger sibling lands on#53945 retains127646464 ✅128649696 ❌16096128128 ❌
With retention keeping only the higher position, every retained state sits above every candidate the resend’s lookup can produce, and the reconciled hit collapses to 0 — the same zero-hit failure sparse retention already avoids at unaligned prompt lengths.
Fix
get_replay_boundary becomes get_replay_boundaries and returns both positions; cache_blocks retains each. Both collapse to a single position whenever the prompt is not block-aligned, so this adds at most one retained state per request.
Because it only ever adds a reachable position, hit length cannot regress. Swept over 136 configurations (prompt lengths 128–392, identical resend and longer sibling, hash block size 16 and 64): 8 cases go from a 0-token hit to a real hit, 0 cases get shorter.
On the alignment
The boundary stays computed at scheduler_block_size, not the finer _cache_hit_alignment_tokens, deliberately. Fine-grained hits extend into the first non-full block only when a partial tail was registered there, so a hash-granular boundary over-estimates how far a lookup reaches and names a position above the real candidate. Measured: doing that regresses prompt lengths 160/176/224/240 from a real hit to 0.
Test Plan
tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_hybrid_mamba_retention_mtp_resend_of_aligned_prompt — a 128-token prompt (exact multiple of the 32-token alignment) with a Mamba “align” MTP group at retention_interval=0, asserting the resend hit and the longer sibling’s hit.
Test Result
Fails on main with assert 0 == 64 — the resend gets no cache hit at all. Passes with this change. tests/v1/core shows no new failures.
Related, not fixed here
OffloadingConnectorScheduler builds its own reachable_boundaries from req.num_prompt_tokens - 1 and never applies the EAGLE drop at all, feeding the same reachable_block_mask. That looks like the same class of bug at a third site, but the offloading path deliberately treats “no annotated eagle group” as non-EAGLE (#52735), so its model differs by design and it deserves its own change rather than a drive-by here.

Rebased onto main, and the PR has been repointed — the description above is rewritten to match.
#53945 landed while this was open and fixes the failure this PR originally targeted, by moving the replay boundary down to the post-drop position instead of retaining an extra state below it. That approach is better than what this PR had, so the old mechanism (reachable_hit_positions, lookup_drops_eagle_block) is gone entirely.
What survives is a narrower bug in that new boundary, found while rebasing. get_replay_boundary computes from floor(num_prompt_tokens / block), but get_computed_blocks caps a lookup at num_tokens - 1 so the last token can be recomputed for logits. A resend of the identical prompt therefore matches one block lower than a sibling whose prompt merely starts with this one, and drops from there. The two positions coincide except when the prompt length is an exact multiple of the scheduler block size — and there, retention keeps only the higher one, so the resend’s every retained state sits above every candidate its lookup can produce and the reconciled hit collapses to 0.
The new test fails on current main with assert 0 == 64 — a total miss on an identical resend of a 128-token prompt.
The fix returns both positions. Since it only ever adds a reachable position, hit length cannot regress; swept over 136 configurations, 8 go from a 0-token hit to a real hit and none get shorter.

#54873 [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Improve QSA sparse GQA for prefill and short-ctx decode
vllm-project/vllm#54873 · gau-nernst · MERGED · created 2026-09-02T02:50:36Z · merged 2026-09-04T13:08:03Z
Purpose
QSA sparse attention read topk indices from [num_tokens, 2048+3] buffer, where each token can attend up to 2048+3 past KV tokens. This number can be smaller when a new token’s position is less than 2048, hence the indices buffer might be padded with -1. This is true for fresh prefill (causal attention) requests and short-context decode.
In the current code, sparse GQA always attend to the full 2048+3 indices (with appropriate masking of course). This is wasteful when there is a lot of padding like mentioned above. To fix this issue, we insert a variable valid_counts, representing the total number of valid, non-padding indices, at the end of the logical_indices table. Why this design?

The valid counts always go together with the indices table. This can be seen as an encoding of variable length sequences with stable buffer size.
This also works nicely with topk indices reuse in MTP compact_topk_indices → we don’t need to carry another tensor and ensure it’s in-sync with the indices table

The key change in the kernel is basically this (notice the loop’s upper bound is tightened by valid_counts)

valid_count = tl.load(indices_ptr + row * stride_indices_row + TOPK)
tile_end = tl.minimum(
  NUM_TILES, tl.cdiv(tl.minimum(valid_count, TOPK), BLOCK_N)
)
for tile in range(split_id, tile_end, NUM_SPLITS):
  ...

#54915 [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Compact indexer logits workspace to improve prefill efficiency
vllm-project/vllm#54915 · gau-nernst · MERGED · created 2026-09-02T07:06:10Z · merged 2026-09-04T07:43:21Z
Purpose
During prefill, we apply chunking on indexer to cap the memory usage consumed by logits workspace. This logits workspace have shape [num_tokens, ctx_len] representing QK product. Currently we size ctx_len based on worst possible case
github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c00091e026709b149d80246a18928f514871c160/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py#L580-L587
Notice columns = page_table.shape[1] * k_cache.shape[1]. Page table accommodates up to max model len size, thus this hugely overestimates the logits workspace. By deriving a lower upper bound based on Python scalar max_seq_len, we can process more tokens per chunk and reduce total number of chunks, thus overall improve GPU efficiency.
This PR also removes  / HEAD_DIM**0.5 in the indexer (both prefill and decode) since the constant normalization factor doesn’t affect topk ranking.

#55027 [Bugfix][KV Connector] MooncakeStore: exclude non-prefix-cacheable (QSA ring) groups; fix align-mode check
vllm-project/vllm#55027 · zhewenl · MERGED · created 2026-09-02T22:12:22Z · merged 2026-09-14T02:18:16Z
Purpose
Fix #54726: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with prefix caching and MooncakeStoreConnector fails because its QSA ring scratch cache is transferable, but is not valid hash-addressed prefix data.
The QSA cache returns a CircularBufferSpec; CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable is explicitly False. Its capacity is 4 without speculative tokens and 8 with MTP=3, while aligned attention/Mamba groups use block size 800. MooncakeStore previously built its hash/store/lookup layout from every enable_kv_transfer=True group, so the ring reached a divisibility check intended only for storable prefix groups.
A second issue was hidden behind that failure: MooncakeStore inferred Mamba align mode by comparing each Mamba block size with the globally rewritten cache_config.block_size. With heterogeneous groups, that global value can differ from the resolved Mamba group size even when mamba_cache_mode is correctly "align".

An extra ~50 GB ngram table for the embedding autotune does not land as a clean CUDA OOM there — it pushes the host into thrash, and userspace stops making progress while the kernel stays up. That is why there is no traceback to attach: no error, no crash, no core. Our supervisor did not fire either, because both its liveness checks needed the host to be able to run bash.
Two things this implies for anyone on unified-memory parts, which I think supports merging this:

The failure is silent and unattended-hostile. A compile-related OOM on a discrete-GPU box gets you an exception and a restart; here it gets you two dead nodes and no signal.
Any autotune or compile step whose peak allocation is a meaningful fraction of total system memory needs to account for host memory on these SKUs, not just free VRAM.

Removing @support_torch_compile for this path takes the whole class of failure off the table for us. Thanks for pushing it through.

#55713 [Spec Decode] Add NVFP4 DSpark gathered top-k projection
vllm-project/vllm#55713 · askliar · MERGED · created 2026-09-07T10:43:37Z · merged 2026-09-09T17:33:47Z
Motivation
DSpark’s Markov head computes the draft correction by selecting rows from its W2 projection. With a quantized W2 Markov head, those rows are stored as packed NVFP4 values plus per-group/global scales, so they cannot be indexed and used as ordinary dense weights. The selected rows must be gathered and dequantized before the correction matmul.
This is required to run nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark, whose Markov head is quantized. Without this path, draft top-k either cannot run or falls back to an incompatible dense-weight assumption.
What changed

Retain packed NVFP4 W2 weights and scales after ModelOpt loading when DSpark draft top-k is enabled.
Add a Triton gathered-row dequantization and bias kernel for CUDA BF16.
Preserve the dequantize/scatter fallback for CPU and CUDA FP16/W4A16 paths.
Add focused parity coverage for the gathered NVFP4 path.

def get_kv_connector_stats(self) -> Optional[HiSparseKVConnectorStats]: ...
and the connector wires it into the standard pipeline:

worker.get_kv_connector_stats()          # HiSparseKVConnectorStats (list of snapshot deltas)

#56227 [Feat][Model] Support encoder-side SWA-bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
vllm-project/vllm#56227 · ivanium · MERGED · created 2026-09-10T07:44:40Z · merged 2026-09-18T22:01:24Z
Purpose
DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps a 128-token sliding-window (SWA) KV cache per layer beside its prefix-cacheable compressed MLA and indexer caches. Storing that window for prefix caching and KV connectors costs more than it saves, so this implements DeepSeek’s encoder-side “SWA bounded replay”: the SWA caches leave prefix caching, and after a prefix hit ending at H the scheduler recomputes the hit’s last window [H-128, H) to rebuild them. The replayed tokens keep their cached KV in every other group, their window attention reads nothing below H-128, and decode always sees a full window. Outputs after a hit are therefore not bit-identical to a cold run, by design.

KV cache spec: SlidingWindowMLASpec(bounded_replay=True) derives prefix_cacheable=False and prefix_replay_tokens=sliding_window; UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs forwards both to the worker.
Scheduler: a hit records Request.replay_start = H-128 and rewinds the computed count by the window; async KV-connector loads replay once the KV arrives; chunks ending inside the replayed range allocate nothing new; hits no longer than the window are not adopted.
Worker: only DeepSeek-V4.1 replays, so DeepseekV41ModelState owns the per-request replay start. add_request stores it; prepare_attn gathers it for the batch’s prefills, pads the replayed tokens’ slots in the prefix-cacheable groups with one Triton kernel, and hands the starts to the sparse SWA metadata builder through a ModelSpecificAttnMetadata. The runner core is untouched apart from an optional model_specific_attn_metadata argument on DefaultModelState.prepare_attn.
DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels clamp the window at replay_start: the SWA index and gather-length kernels, the FlashInfer mixed index kernel and the FlashMLA combine kernel. The compressed slot mappings (MLA and indexer) inherit the padding of the tokens’ own slots, so a replayed token never re-enters the compressed caches.
Switch: --swa-bounded-replay (CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay, default on), read by the V4.1 attention layer. Needs model runner V2 and no prefill context parallelism; otherwise it logs once and keeps the SWA cache in prefix caching.
One bugfix rides along as its own commit: KV-connector hits are taken in whole blocks under replay.

Known gap: a running request restarted in place under kv_load_failure_policy=recompute keeps its worker-side replay boundary and would recompute with a stale clamp; a follow-up will preempt such requests instead. No other open PR implements SWA replay.
Usage
Nothing to configure: DeepSeek-V4.1 replays by default on model runner V2. --no-swa-bounded-replay restores the previous behaviour (SWA KV stored in the prefix cache). With replay on, KV connectors transfer only the MLA and indexer caches, and hits of at most 128 tokens are not adopted.

#56254 [DSA] Wire DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits into the DeepSeek V4.1 indexer
vllm-project/vllm#56254 · JaredforReal · MERGED · created 2026-09-10T10:27:08Z · merged 2026-09-15T21:07:15Z
Purpose
DeepSeek V4.1 selects attention tokens in two levels: one indexer layer publishes the top candidate blocks of the context, and the indexer layers after it pick their top-k inside those blocks. Today the consumer layers still score the whole context with dense MQA logits and then mask everything outside the candidates. DeepGEMM 2.8 ships sparse MQA-logits kernels (deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#432) that score only a given list of blocks, so this PR lets the consumer layers score just the candidate blocks. Their logits work goes from O(context) to O(candidate blocks), a fixed 16K positions for V4.1-Flash, and their top-k runs in that compressed space and is mapped back to context positions.
Design:

A separate indexer, not a branch in the dense one. The consumer layers use a new SparseMQAIndexer layer with its own backend and attention metadata (DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend, DeepseekV41SparseIndexerMetadata). It is a plain module rather than a custom op: V4.1 does not go through torch.compile, and the attention layer already runs the indexer inside its breakable-CUDA-graph eager segment. The dense SparseAttnIndexer op is untouched. The candidate-source layer and the indexers before it stay dense.
Every requirement is checked once, at engine start. The metadata builder validates the model, the MXFP4 indexer cache, the GPU generation, the DeepGEMM version, the DeepSelect extension and the logits/top-k layout it needs, and raises a clear error instead of silently falling back per step. There is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path: the candidate expansion and the index remap are Triton kernels, the top-k is DeepSelect.
Nothing is allocated or recomputed on the hot path. The builder owns the per-row scratch; the candidate-block expansion and the DeepGEMM schedule depend only on the candidates, which are identical for all consumer layers of a step, so the first consumer computes them and the others reuse them through the shared metadata.
No dtype casts on the hot path. The sparse kernels take bf16 weights and emit bf16 logits. The fused Q RoPE-quant kernel that produces the per-head weights writes them in bf16 for this indexer (fp32 for the dense one), and DeepSelect (#56464) runs the top-k on the bf16 logits directly.
Opt-in via --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4", "indexer_sparse_logits": true}'. Below ~16K tokens the candidates cover the whole context and the dense path is cheaper, so the default stays off; the feature is for long-context serving.

Opt-in via --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4", "indexer_sparse_logits": true}'. Below ~16K tokens the candidates cover the whole context and the dense path is cheaper, so the default stays off; the feature is for long-context serving.
One KV-layout requirement. DeepGEMM’s paged kernels address pages as base + page * stride and need that stride 512B-aligned. In V4.1’s block-major layout the stride is the whole block (all layers’ pages), which is not 512-aligned. #56387 [Bugfix][Spec Decode][MoE] Avoid uninitialized EPLB state in DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark drafter
vllm-project/vllm#56387 · luoyuctl · MERGED · created 2026-09-11T03:26:33Z · merged 2026-09-15T14:35:48Z
Purpose
Fix DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark startup when EPLB is enabled for the target model.
The target and DSpark draft use different routed-expert topologies (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target: 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter: 128). When target-model EPLB is enabled, the draft routers inherit enable_eplb=True, but the drafter is not registered with a compatible EPLB model state. Its router-level EplbLayerState therefore never receives expert_load_view / logical-to-physical mappings and profiling fails with:

ValueError: EPLB requires expert_load_view != None
Fix

Keep EPLB enabled for the target model.
Apply the override in the shared load_dspark_model() path while constructing the draft ParallelConfig.
Use shallow config replace() calls only; do not deep-copy the full VllmConfig after target-model construction.
Disable draft EPLB, redundant experts, and elastic EP atomically in the same ParallelConfig replacement.
Preserve the target config and shared runtime/compilation state.
Add a focused regression test for atomic target/draft parallel-config isolation.

This intentionally disables EPLB for DSpark draft models while leaving target EPLB unchanged. Full heterogeneous target/draft EPLB support belongs in the EPLB multi-model machinery and should be handled separately.

#56429 Revert “[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode (#53664)”
vllm-project/vllm#56429 · shen-shanshan · MERGED · created 2026-09-11T08:48:23Z · merged 2026-09-11T16:17:26Z
Purpose
This PR reverts #53664 (“[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode”). That PR added a fallback in MLAAttentionLayer.build() that derives dcp_local_seq_lens from seq_lens whenever CommonAttentionMetadata does not carry it, together with an assert and two test-registry entries. The fallback is dead code: in vLLM’s in-tree paths, dcp_local_seq_lens is always populated before the MLA decode path runs whenever DCP is enabled.
Evidence:

The monolithic V1 model runner populates CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens unconditionally when decode_context_parallel_size > 1 (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2456-2466), and this has been in place since before #53664 was authored.
The modular model runner (MRV2) does the same via maybe_prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens() right before attention metadata is built, after PCP batch partitioning (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1728, helper in vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py). The helper returns None only when dcp_size == 1, in which case the MLA layer’s dcp_world_size is also 1 and the branch is never taken, so the fallback is unreachable.
Both runners always set seq_lens on CommonAttentionMetadata, so the assert added by #53664 is likewise unreachable.

Keeping the fallback would also mask future regressions in runner-side population: if a path ever stopped populating dcp_local_seq_lens, the layer would silently derive it instead of failing loudly. Removing it restores a single source of truth for DCP-local sequence lengths (the model runner). The two test-registry entries added by #53664 are removed along with the revert.

1. Zero query heads should keep the warp-per-slot grid
launchFusedDeepseekV4Templated<..., 0, ...> fell through to the reduced-grid kernel above NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF. That grid earns its keep by iterating a token’s Q heads inside one CTA — with zero Q slots there is nothing to iterate, so it launches one block per token and if (warpId < slot_end) leaves seven of every eight warps with no work.
Launch overhead hides this up to roughly 16k tokens in a single insert, which is why the microbenchmarks in the description don’t show it. Past that it costs about 2x. One GB300, packed uint8 record, eager, microseconds:

The bound cache already is [num_blocks, block_size, bytes_per_token], so its last dimension is the record width — which also makes the reshape a no-op, so that goes too.
The reason to prefer the tensor is that the attribute name is not stable: it has to become swa_bytes_per_token once a layer’s sliding-window and compressed records can differ in width, which is exactly what an NVFP4 compressed record needs. stream. @eager_break_during_capture keeps the side-stream work out of
captured graphs, and persistent per-layer staging buffers keep
addresses stable across replays. DBO and microbatching are not supported

#56633 [Perf][DSv4.1] Fold the mHC post block into the delayed pre projection
vllm-project/vllm#56633 · zyongye · MERGED · created 2026-09-12T19:28:52Z · merged 2026-09-14T18:57:39Z
Purpose
DeepSeek-V4.1 runs an mHC post block and then the next sublayer’s delayed pre block at every seam. Each seam therefore pays for three things: a post kernel, a split-k projection that re-reads the residual streams the post kernel just wrote, and the pre epilogue.
DSv4 already avoids the middle read: mhc_fused_tilelang computes the updated residual in registers and feeds the pre-norm GEMM from there. V4.1 could not reuse it, for the same reason it needed its own pre in the first place — it collapses each sublayer’s input with the previous sublayer’s pre-mix and hands the next one back, and the DSv4 fused wrapper neither accepts an incoming pre-mix nor returns one.
Approach
mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_tilelang runs the existing fused kernel and then the delayed pre epilogue (MHC_PRE_NORM_KERNEL, use_pre_mix_in / save_pre_mix), returning (residual, post_mix, comb_mix, layer_input, next_pre_mix). Above the fused kernel’s token range it falls back to exactly today’s mhc_post_tilelang + split-k GEMM, so only the small-batch path changes shape.
Both V4.1 seams route through it, except one:

Attention seam — fuses, unless Engram is injected. Engram reads the residual between the post and the pre, so the post cannot move into the projection there; that branch keeps the separate kernels.
FFN seam — always fuses.
DSpark draft reuses DeepseekV4DecoderLayer, so it inherits both.

Attention seam — fuses, unless Engram is injected. Engram reads the residual between the post and the pre, so the post cannot move into the projection there; that branch keeps the separate kernels.
FFN seam — always fuses.
DSpark draft reuses DeepseekV4DecoderLayer, so it inherits both.

#56794 [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Keep transient checkpoints out of prefix-cache eviction
vllm-project/vllm#56794 · Sy0307 · MERGED · created 2026-09-14T08:57:34Z · merged 2026-09-15T06:18:25Z
Summary
Keep transient KDA/Mamba prefill checkpoints out of the ordinary prefix-cache eviction set when sparse retention is explicitly active.
This change targets Kimi-K3’s hybrid attention path.
Problem
FlashKDA creates internal checkpoints so the current prefill can continue from a recurrent-state boundary without an additional scheduling step. A checkpoint in the middle of a prompt is useful to the current request, but it is not necessarily a reusable shared-prefix boundary.
Before this change, such a checkpoint could be re-keyed and registered as a normal prefix-cache block. It then participated in the same GPU LRU eviction pool as reusable hot prefixes:

middle checkpoint -> hash -> prefix-cache LRU -> evicts hot prefix
                                             -> later local hit becomes a miss
                                             -> extra load or prefill work
Before/after cache lifecycle:

Before:
 
  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint
      |        |
      |        +--> hash + ordinary LRU
      |                     |
      |                     +--> competes with hot prefix
      |                                  |
      |                                  +--> local prefix miss
 
After:
 
  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint ------------------> current request can use it
      |                                              |
      |                                              +--> no ordinary LRU entry
      |
      +--> shared-prefix-boundary checkpoint ------> reusable prefix cache
                                                     |
                                                     +--> may be retained/shared
This is particularly problematic when prefix_cache_retention_interval == 0: intermediate checkpoints are not intended to be retained as dense semantic checkpoints, but their temporary hash could still make them eviction candidates.
Fix
Pass the active retention interval into checkpoint publication. When sparse retention is active and the checkpoint is neither at the end of the prompt nor at the shared-prefix boundary, treat it as request-local state:

middle checkpoint -> current request may use it
                  -> temporary hash is removed
                  -> no ordinary prefix-cache LRU entry
                  -> reusable hot prefixes remain protected
Prompt-end and shared-prefix-boundary checkpoints retain the existing publication behavior. This change does not disable KDA checkpoint computation or change the state written by FlashKDA.
Performance
On a representative B200 Kimi-K3 hybrid workload using TP8/PP2/direct DCP8, the isolated production-style comparison was:



Configuration
Output throughput




Checkpoint disabled (diagnostic baseline)
1013.00 tokens/s


Checkpoint enabled with transient-checkpoint retention fix
1091.80 tokens/s



The fixed configuration improved throughput by 7.78% over the checkpoint-disabled diagnostic baseline while retaining the internal checkpoint feature. A separate run with the GEMM-AR option disabled measured 1108.89 tokens/s; that result is included only as context and is not an isolated measurement of this patch.
These measurements are workload-specific and are not used as a claim that this small cache-lifecycle change explains every difference between software stacks. The primary regression signal is the cache-manager reproduction: temporary checkpoint publication changes which blocks compete in the local prefix-cache eviction pool.
Why this is not a duplicate

PR #55760 changes the default sparse/dense retention policy for Mamba + EAGLE; this change keeps the explicit sparse-retention behavior but fixes transient checkpoint publication.
PR #56615 fixes MooncakeStore boundary pairing between Mamba/KDA and attention KV; this change is limited to local prefix-cache block retention.
PR #56525 guards cache hits until the writing scheduler step is committed; this change addresses eviction eligibility, not write visibility.
PR #52527 adds observability for sparse-retention misses; this change modifies the cache lifecycle.

Validation
Focused prefix-cache tests should be run with:

pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
The change is intentionally small and preserves the current-request checkpoint path. Model-scale performance validation is still required on a representative hybrid KDA workload.

#56881 [Kimi-K3] Use the fused K/V pack kernel on the decode-context-parallel prefill path
vllm-project/vllm#56881 · brandonfzhang · MERGED · created 2026-09-14T18:28:42Z · merged 2026-10-06T00:13:56Z
Purpose
Kimi-K3 prefill with a long context runs in chunks. For every chunk of every MLA layer, the model projects the gathered latent cache into per-head keys and values, casts them to FP8, and lays them out as the contiguous key and value tensors the attention kernel expects.
#51772 fused that cast-and-layout step into one kernel (fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat_quant_fp8, or fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat for a bf16 query) for the normal prefill path, but left decode context parallelism (DCP) out of scope. With decode_context_parallel_size > 1 the Kimi-K3 layer delegates chunked-context prefill to the shared MLA implementation, whose per-chunk tail still does the work as four separate PyTorch operations: two FP8 casts and two strided slice copies.
This PR routes the DCP path through the same fused kernels the non-DCP path already uses.
What changes

MLACommonImpl._context_parallel_compute_prefill_context takes an optional fused_mla_kv_concat_fn(kv_nope, k_pe, use_fp8_prefill) -> (k, v). When it is given it replaces the cast + split + concat tail; when it is not, the method runs exactly the statements it runs today. No other model passes it.
MultiHeadLatentAttention (Kimi-K3) passes self._fused_mla_kv_concat, which makes the same two kernel calls its non-DCP loop already makes.

MLACommonImpl._context_parallel_compute_prefill_context takes an optional fused_mla_kv_concat_fn(kv_nope, k_pe, use_fp8_prefill) -> (k, v). When it is given it replaces the cast + split + concat tail; when it is not, the method runs exactly the statements it runs today. No other model passes it.
MultiHeadLatentAttention (Kimi-K3) passes self._fused_mla_kv_concat, which makes the same two kernel calls its non-DCP loop already makes.

No new environment variables, no runtime signature probing, no logging: the fused kernels are what every Kimi-K3 deployment already runs on the non-DCP path, so the DCP path simply follows it.
Microbenchmark: fused kernel vs. the stock tail, across shapes
Per reviewer request, the fused kernel was timed against the stock four-operation tail over every local head count Kimi-K3 can have (96 heads / TP) and chunk sizes from 1 to 131072 tokens, on three GPUs. Cold L2 (a 256 MB buffer is cleared before every call), median of 100 CUDA-event timings, outputs checked byte-exact against the stock path on every row before timing (all exact, no mismatches). Numbers are stock_us / fused_us; vLLM 0.31.0 release wheel, torch 2.13 + CUDA 13.0.
H100 NVL (SM90), FP8 KV cache + FP8 prefill query (the production Kimi-K3 configuration):

RTX 5080 (SM120, Blackwell), FP8 path: geomean 1.32x, min 1.11x (at 1536 tokens / 48 heads), no row below 1.0x; FP8 rope key: geomean 1.30x, min 1.06x.
L40S (SM89, below the kernel’s SM90 target, included for completeness): FP8 path geomean 1.42x, min 1.02x, no row below 1.0x; FP8 rope key: geomean 1.44x, min 1.05x. Only the bf16-query path on this card has rows below 1.0x (worst 0.91x, at 512 to 16384 tokens with 48 to 96 heads); that path is bf16 cache + bf16 query, which no Kimi-K3 deployment on Ada would run, and the non-DCP path already takes it unconditionally.
GB300 (SM103), the production deployment container (vLLM nightly, torch 2.13 + CUDA 13.0), FP8 path, same head-by-token grid, cold L2, median of 100, byte-exact on every row:

Geomean 6.48x, min 3.70x, no row below 1.0x. Absolute times at TP8 (12 heads): 1536 tokens 96 us → 11 us; 16384 tokens 157 us → 37 us; 65536 tokens 582 us → 120 us. The small-chunk ratios are large because the stock tail is four eager launches (about 85 to 90 us of fixed cost on this host) while the fused kernel is one.
Conclusion: the fused kernel is faster than the stock tail on every Kimi-K3 shape on every GPU on which the FP8 path is deployed (3.7x or more on GB300, 2x or more on H100), so no shape heuristic is added. The gain is bandwidth: the stock tail writes and re-reads an FP8 copy of the whole projection output; the fused kernel reads it once and writes the two outputs directly.

Benchmark script (stand-alone; run inside a vLLM install)

  return statistics.median(t)
 
 
l2 = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device='cuda')
for H in (96, 48, 24, 12, 6):
  for T in (1, 16, 128, 512, 1536, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072):
    kv = torch.randn(T, H, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
    pe = torch.randn(T, 1, ROPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
    (k0, v0), (k1, v1) = stock_fp8(kv, pe), fused_fp8(kv, pe)
    assert torch.equal(k0.view(torch.uint8), k1.view(torch.uint8))
    assert torch.equal(v0.view(torch.uint8), v1.view(torch.uint8))
    a, b = (
      time_cold(lambda: stock_fp8(kv, pe), l2),
      time_cold(lambda: fused_fp8(kv, pe), l2),
    )
    print(f'H={H:3d} T={T:6d} stock={a:8.1f}us fused={b:8.1f}us {a / b:.2f}x')

End-to-end
Kimi-K3 FP4 on two GB300 nodes (TP8 x DCP8, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM ragged prefill backend), 3600-second agentic-coding replay at 70 concurrent sessions, same build on both sides except for this routing. Across three paired runs of this A/B the fused pack improved p90 normalized interactivity by 6 to 11% and p90 inter-token latency by about 7%. Throughput moved between -0.6% and +9.2% across those runs, which is inside the roughly 5% run-to-run drift we measured for identical builds on this route, so we do not claim a throughput win; the robust gain is in the latency tail, which is where long multi-chunk requests live.
Accuracy. GSM8K-style probes use prompts far shorter than the scheduler chunk and never reach the DCP context path, so we ran a paired teacher-forced perplexity test on ten public-domain texts of 30k to 36k tokens each (330,944 tokens total), scored token by token on a server with the fused pack and one on the stock tail: perplexity 1.014803 vs 1.014815 (-0.0012%), 19 top-1 flips out of 330,944, consistent with batching nondeterminism between two independent server starts. The kernel output itself is byte-identical to the stock tail (checked on every microbenchmark row above and in the unit test).

vllm-project/vllm#56893 · zyongye · MERGED · created 2026-09-14T20:31:07Z · merged 2026-09-15T03:12:56Z
Purpose
DeepSeek-V4.1 has been reusing DeepSeek-V4’s paged fp8_ds_mla record. FlashMLA has a V4.1-specific one that quantizes the RoPE dims too; this switches DeepSeek-V4.1 onto it on SM100.






























V4 (ModelType::V4)V4.1 (ModelType::V41)data row448 B fp8 e4m3 NoPE + 128 B bf16 RoPE512 B fp8 e4m3, RoPE includedscale row7 UE8M0 of 64 dims + 1 pad byte16 UE8M0, one per 32 dims (MXFP8)bytes/token584528page (TMA) stride576 B512 B
Both records put a page’s whole data region ahead of its whole scale region, so a page is block_size * bytes_per_token rounded up to the TMA stride. Because block_size is always a multiple of 32, every V4.1 page is an exact multiple of 512 — the padding the V4 record needed disappears, on top of the 9.6% smaller record.
Gated on SM100: ModelType::V41 is absent from FlashMLA’s SM90 sparse-decode feature set, so SM90, ROCm and the FlashInfer SM120 path keep the V4 record. No new cache dtype and no new flag — --kv-cache-dtype fp8 resolves to fp8_ds_mla as before and the record follows the arch, exactly as fp8_ds_mla already means 656 B for V3.2 and 584 B for V4.
What changed

FlashMLA pin → vllm-project/FlashMLA@b6ef01c, following the fork’s tree reorganization (csrc/sm* → csrc/kernels/sm*, API implementations split into .cpp files). api.cpp now registers fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_* and the two permute kernels, so their instantiations must be compiled for _flashmla_C to link; the source list mirrors the fork’s setup.py minus the dense backward, which is training-only.
Writers: the fused SWA insert takes a kv_mxfp8 argument (one UE8M0 scale per lane pair instead of per four, and the RoPE lanes quantize instead of storing bf16); the compressed-cache insert gets an MXFP8 kernel that applies RoPE before choosing scales, since the RoPE dims are now quantized.
Readers: the Triton gather and the CuteDSL gather are parameterized by record instead of hard-coded to 448/64, and both pick it from k_cache.shape[-1] — the per-token width the KV cache spec already publishes — so the V4 record keeps working unchanged on the same code path.

The indexer page has to move with them
_get_bytes_per_block makes a block’s stride the sum of every page in the group, and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 packs the SWA cache, the compressed-KV cache, the indexer cache and the compressor ring into one block. Divisibility by the TMA stride therefore only holds if every contributing page carries the same padding — which is what the indexer cache’s 576 B alignment was for, rather than any constraint of its own kernel.
Leaving the indexer at 576 while the main caches moved to 512 produced a block stride of 212160 (a multiple of neither) and tripped FlashMLA’s block_stride_bytes % TMA_K_STRIDE == 0 assertion in the startup profile run, after a clean weight load. Every per-spec page size looked correct in isolation. This PR ties the indexer’s alignment to the same gate.

#56935 [Model][DSv4.1] FlashMLA mega attention and the NVFP4 compressed KV cache
vllm-project/vllm#56935 · zyongye · MERGED · created 2026-09-15T03:21:41Z · merged 2026-09-16T10:07:51Z
Purpose
Supersedes #56344, which closed when its base branch dsv41-optimized was deleted.
FlashMLA’s mega-attention kernel does Q RoPE, sparse attention, the output’s inverse RoPE and its FP8 cast in one launch, writing straight into the buffer wo_a consumes. It arrives as FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend (FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41) with its own attention layer, plus the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV record that only this kernel can read — and, as of this revision, it is the SM100 default rather than an opt-in backend.
Rebased onto current main, which now includes #56441 (KV-only DSpark context insertion); that PR touched the same translation unit and its interaction with this one is described under _Rebase onto 56441_ below.
The interface capability the base layer acts on
accepts_unnormed_unroped_query — the attention kernel applies the Q norm and RoPE itself and reads Q in its own chunk-interleaved layout, so the layer’s fused KV insert reduces to a zero-pad of Q to the kernel’s head count, and to nothing at all once the shard is already that wide.
The output side needs no flag: the mega layer’s _alloc_attn_out / _o_proj pair speaks QuantizedActivation where every other layer speaks bf16 and rotates in _o_proj. An earlier revision of this PR declared a second capability, produces_inv_roped_quantized_output; it had no reader — the dispatch is the override pair — so it is gone.
Q reaches the kernel through the existing fused op, not a new one
Rather than a separate Triton pad kernel, fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert gains two independent knobs:

apply_q_rope — rotate Q as well; KV is always rotated. A runtime argument, on the kv_mxfp8 precedent.
is_q_interleaved — read and write Q in the mega layout (32 chunks of [heads, 16] per token), which moves the padding heads to the tail of every head-dim chunk. A template parameter, because it selects the address arithmetic.

They are orthogonal, and that is tested. A lane owns dims [16l, 16l+16) of its head in either layout — only the address differs — so the per-head RMSNorm and the GPT-J RoPE are equally valid interleaved. test_q_interleaved_is_orthogonal_to_norm_and_rope pins it over all eight of (16, 64 heads) × (norm on/off) × (RoPE on/off): the head-major result permuted into the interleaved layout must equal the interleaved path on a permuted input, bit for bit, with the KV cache byte-identical so the Q layout cannot leak into the KV half. An earlier revision conflated the two into one flag on the mistaken belief that the layout made RoPE ill-defined; that test fails against the conflated form.
q_head_padded = 0 additionally asks for the KV insert alone, which is what TP1 wants — its 64 live heads are already the kernel’s head count, so no Q pass is scheduled at all.
One buffer pair per step
The output travels as a QuantizedActivation (kMxfp8Dynamic: fp8 e4m3 data, packed-ue8m0 MN-major scales). FlashMLA’s fused ops take caller-provided out_fp8 / out_sf, so a single buffer pair covers a whole step: the prefill chunks and the decode segment fill disjoint token ranges, and one fp8_einsum over all N tokens replaces one call per segment. The scale buffer’s head-dim stride is ceil4(N) — both what the kernel requires of a caller buffer and what DeepGEMM expects for that N.
wq_b rows and wo_a columns are permuted once at load into the kernel’s chunk-interleaved layouts, so the surrounding GEMMs speak them directly rather than shuffling per step. DSpark’s draft layers are ordinary DeepseekV4DecoderLayers and therefore take the engine-wide backend, so they owe the same post-load permutation; DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading now runs it, where before it finalized only MoE weights and every draft forward hit the layer’s own guard.
NVFP4 compressed cache

DSpark’s draft layers are ordinary DeepseekV4DecoderLayers and therefore take the engine-wide backend, so they owe the same post-load permutation; DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading now runs it, where before it finalized only MoE weights and every draft forward hit the layer’s own guard.
NVFP4 compressed cache
nvfp4_ds_mla now means the V4.1 MXFP8 sliding-window record beside a 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (256 B of e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales of 16 dims). It rides the byte-width dispatch the fp8 records already use, so rope_quant_insert and dequantize_and_gather_k_cache pick it up with no call-site change; CuteDSL has no fp4 gather, so that record takes Triton.
This is the format the reference implementation itself stores: inference/model.py quantizes the compressed latent with fp4_act_quant(latent, 16, True, scale_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn) — group 16, e4m3 scales. fp8_ds_mla is more precise than the reference on that cache, not less.

Default backend on SM100
An unspecified --attention_config.backend now resolves to FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 on SM100. The layer answers is_available_for() rather than letting the selector guess, because __init__ raises on topologies the kernel cannot serve — it is SM100 only, it needs WV_GROUP_SIZE heads per wo_a group, and a build may not carry the kernel at all. On a 64-head model that admits TP1 through TP8 and declines TP16 (4 local heads), which falls through to FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 instead of failing at startup.
The default is chosen for TP1’s win plus the 45%-smaller compressed record, not for a uniform speedup — see the table below, where TP2 through TP8 are a wash. Set --attention_config.backend=FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 to get the previous path.

The decisive variable is live heads over padded heads, not batch size: the kernel absorbs the inverse RoPE and the FP8 cast, whose cost scales with live heads, while its own cost scales with padded heads — always 64, since FlashMLA’s FP8 decode takes only h_q in {64, 128}. So TP1 wins and TP2 down cancel to within a few percent. There is no batch size at which falling back pays, so there is no minimum-token threshold and no fallback path to maintain.
An earlier revision of this table also charged the mega arm for a separate Q-pad kernel “that the split-KV path gets for free”; that is no longer true — the pad is now inside the same fused insert both paths run, and at TP1 it is skipped entirely.
These are decode numbers; prefill is unmeasured. Measure under CUDA graphs — in eager mode launch overhead swamps both paths and overstates the fused one several-fold.

Summary
incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash. On current main the pair cannot be served: vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}' fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.
The three blockers on main (9d4d9aa), in the order they surface:

#StageError on mainRoot cause1draft model loadRuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interfaceGlm5NextForCausalLM / Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare SupportsEagle3, and Glm5NextModel is not an EagleModelMixin, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]).2KV cache initNotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers._get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft’s sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640).3configValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabledcreate_draft_parallel_config copies enable_expert_parallel from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter).
Changes

vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py (aux hidden-state capture). Glm5NextModel becomes an EagleModelMixin; Glm5NextForCausalLM and Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration declare SupportsEagle3. The tensor handed to the drafter is not hidden_states + residual: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer’s hc_post into the next layer’s fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary residual is the widened (T, 4 * hidden) stream (a naive hidden + residual fails with The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1) and hidden_states alone is the raw layer output. _aux_hidden_state() completes the deferred hc_post through a dedicated MHCPostOp and contracts the streams back to hidden_size with hc_contract, which is the quantity SGLang’s _prepare_aux_hidden_state feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original (hidden_states, residual, post, comb) tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in hidden_states and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, forward returns (hidden_states, aux_hidden_states); otherwise the return type is unchanged.
